title: III. In the Old Testament Ecclesiastes 12:7 is most clear; dust and spirit opposed (Augustine)
pass_a_gloss: But the soul, produced not from any matter but from nothing, when it returns has nowhere to return except toward the author who gave it, as Augustine writes in On Genesis Literally book 10. The body indeed, made from soil and matter, returns or stands as resolved into that very thing from which it stood as made — that is, it perishes. Here body and spirit or the rational soul stand as opposed: and as they stand as belonging toward diverse nature and origin, so also they obtain a diverse exit. III. In the Old Testament that belonging toward Ecclesiastes 12:7 stands as most clear: the dust will return toward the earth as it was, but the spirit will return toward God who gave it.
pass_b_english: III. In the Old Testament that of Ecclesiastes 12:7 is most clear: the dust (the body produced from dust) will return to the earth as it was (what was made from earth ought to return into earth), but the spirit will return to God who gave it. Here body and spirit or the rational soul are opposed: and as they are of diverse nature and origin, so also they obtain a diverse exit. The body indeed, made from soil and matter, returns or is resolved into that very thing from which it was made — that is, it perishes. But the soul, produced not from any matter but from nothing, when it returns has nowhere to return except to the author who gave it, as Augustine writes in On Genesis Literally book 10.
source_text: III. In V. T. maxime perspicuum est illud Eccles. 12.v.7. redibit pulver (corpus e pulvere productum) in terram, quemadmodum fuit, (e terra factum in terram reverti oportet) spiritus autem redibit ad Deum, qui dedit ipsum. Hic opponuntur corpus & spiritus sive anima rationalis: & sicut sunt diversae naturae atque originis, ita & diversum exitum sortiuntur. Corpus quidem ex humo & materia factum, in hoc ipsum, ex quo factum, redit sive resolvitur, i.e. interit. Anima vero non ex aliqua materia, sed e nihilo producta, cum redit, non habet, quo redeat, nisi ad autorem, qui eam dedit, ut scribit Augustinus lib. 10. de Genesi ad literam.
